aboutIntro.headline: “BREAKING NEWS: JOHN SAJU HAS A SLIGHT OBSESSION WITH MAKING THINGS MAKE SENSE.”
aboutIntro.short: John Saju is a UX and service designer who likes taking messy problems and making them clear. He started in animation, pays close attention to detail, and has little patience for unnecessary complexity.

aboutArticle.headline: LOCAL DESIGNER CAUGHT TURNING PROBLEMS INTO PIXELS

about: BELFAST, NORTHERN IRELAND. John Saju keeps poking at everyday problems and asking, “Surely there’s a better way to do this?” Experts call it a convenient career choice. He has a background in Animation & Visual Effects and a Master’s in User Experience & Service Design, and these days he works with user flows instead of timelines, wireframes instead of keyframes, and a tidy Figma file instead of the occasional existential crisis. His work sits somewhere between design, storytelling and technology, and what he cares about most is making digital things that are useful and also nice to use.

aboutSubsections.heading: FROM KEYFRAMES TO USER FLOWS
aboutSubsections.text: Before UX, John spent his days making things move. Animation, visual effects, motion graphics and video editing taught him about composition, storytelling and the small details most people ignore. Somewhere along the way he got more curious about why people use things the way they do, and the move into UX and service design felt natural. Research, strategy and visual design now sit side by side in his work. Apps, websites or whole services, he likes getting stuck into a messy problem and working at it until it makes sense.

aboutSubsections.heading: DESIGNER, STORYTELLER & PART-TIME PIXEL POLICE
aboutSubsections.text: When he isn't nudging a button three pixels to the left, John is usually drawing, editing videos, trying out ideas, or telling himself this is finally the right font. He works in Figma, Framer, Webflow and After Effects. His approach is simple: understand the people, question the obvious, make it look good, and never underestimate a really satisfying interaction. He's taking on interesting problems, big ideas and projects worth losing sleep over.
